in_hebrew.name: יוליאן
in_hebrew.meaning: יוליאן הוא שם נוצרי המורכב מגרעין שם האב יוליוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יוליאן הוא שם נוצרי המורכב מגרעין שם האב יוליוס, שמקורו בשם הלטיני יוליוס, המקורב לשם העברי יואל, שהוא שם נביא, וכן לשם היווני Ιουλιος, שהוא שם נביא. במסורת הנוצרית, יוליאן מיוחס לפטרוס הקדוש, והוא מופיע בדוקומנטים קדומים של הכנסייה. בהקשר של שמות נוצריים, יוליאן מסמל סגירה, אדישות, ואופטימיות, והוא נחשב לשם נאות לילד גבר.

in_greek.name: Ιουλιανός
in_greek.meaning: ο Ιουλιανός είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που αποτελείται από την ρίζα του ονόματος Ιουλιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: ο Ιουλιανός είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που αποτελείται από την ρίζα του ονόματος Ιουλιανός, που προέρχεται από το όνομα Ιουλιανός, που είναι μια λεξη ελληνική που σημαίνει «υπηρέτης του Ιούλιου». Στην ελληνική μυθολογία, ο Ιουλιανός ήταν ο ανδριάς της θεάς Αφροδίτης. Στην Βίβλο, ο Ιουλιανός δεν εμφανίζεται, αλλά το όνομα έχει ιστορία στην αρχαία χριστιανική εκκλησία. Στη μορφή Ιουλιανός, το όνομα Ιουλιανός χρησιμοποιήθηκε για να τιμήσει τους αγίους, ιδιαίτερα τον Αγιο Ιουλιανό, ο οποίος ήταν επίσκοπος της Αλεξάνδρειας τον 5ο αιώνα. Στη σύγχρονη εποχή, το όνομα Ιουλιανός είναι ένα σπάνιο όνομα που συνδέεται με την αρχαιότητα και την εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Iulianus
in_latin.meaning: Iulianus est nomen christianum, quod radicem habet ex nomine Iuliano
in_latin.long_meaning: Iulianus est nomen christianum, quod radicem habet ex nomine Iuliano, auctoritate Iulii Caesaris, Imperatoris Romani, qui nomen suum deducit a Deo Iove. In traditione Christiana, Iulianus attribuitur Petro Apostolo, et in documentis antiquis Ecclesiae apparit. In contextu nominum Christianorum, Iulianus significat defensio, indifferens, et optimista; et reputatur nomen convenientissimum pueri masculini.

in_english.name: Iulian
in_english.meaning: Iulian is a Christian name derived from the Latin name Julian, related to the Hebrew name Yuel and the Greek name Iulios
in_english.long_meaning: Iulian is a Christian name derived from the Latin name Julian, related to the Hebrew name Yuel and the Greek name Iulios, which mean 'upholder of Jupiter'. In Christian tradition, Iulian is associated with Saint Peter, and it appears in early Christian documents. As a Christian name, Iulian symbolizes resolve, indifference, and optimism, making it a suitable name for a boy. In modern times, Iulian is a rare name with ancient roots and ecclesiastical significance, reflecting the rich history of Christianity.

saint_reference.note: Saint Julian was a 5th-century bishop of Alexandria, known for his piety and wisdom.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Iulian" originated from the Roman family name Iulius. This name was a common one among the Roman nobility, as it was believed to be a sign of divine descent from Jupiter, the king of the gods. The name spread beyond the Roman Empire due to the conquests and colonization efforts of Rome.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name "Iulian" is particularly resonant due to Saint Julian of Le Mans. He is a revered bishop and martyr who lived during the late 3rd and early 4th centuries. According to legend, Julian was born into a pagan family but was converted to Christianity after a vision of the Virgin Mary. He went on to perform numerous miracles and was eventually martyred for his faith. Thus, the name "Iulian" carries a profound spiritual significance for many Christians, symbolizing faith, miracles, and the power of divine intervention.

historical_references.reference: Iulian the Apostate was a Roman Emperor who ruled from 360 to 363 AD. He was the last pagan emperor of the Roman Empire. In an attempt to reunite the empire and restore traditional Roman religion, he issued edicts ordering the destruction of Christian churches and the persecution of Christians.
historical_references.context: Last pagan Roman Emperor, attempted to restore traditional Roman religion

historical_references.reference: Saint Julian of Le Mans was a bishop who lived around 305 AD. He was a soldier who was converted to Christianity by a miraculous healing. He was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution for refusing to offer a sacrifice to pagan gods.
historical_references.context: Early Christian martyr, soldier converted to Christianity
